title: The November Heater Failure
background: A residential lease agreement in a cold climate where the heating system failed during a temperature drop.
facts: 1. On November 1st, Marcus notified Elena via text that the heater was not working.
2. Elena replied on November 1st that a technician would arrive on November 3rd.
3. Marcus missed the technician's appointment on November 3rd because he was at work.
4. Elena did not notify Marcus that the technician had arrived and left.
5. On November 5th, Marcus sent an email calling Elena 'negligent' and 'unprofessional'.
6. Elena scheduled a second repair for November 7th.
7. Marcus purchased a portable space heater for $80 on November 8th without consulting Elena.
8. Marcus deducted $80 from the November rent payment.
9. Elena refused to accept the partial rent payment.
dispute: Marcus wants a rent credit for the space heater and a formal apology; Elena wants the full $80 rent balance paid immediately.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the first repair visit and sent a rude email; Elena failed to coordinate the technician's arrival and ignored the initial failure for several days.

title: The Unsanctioned Sublet Dispute
background: Marcus has a one-year lease for an apartment owned by Mrs. Gable.
facts: The lease agreement states that subletting requires written consent from the landlord.
Marcus notified Mrs. Gable via email on June 1st that he needed to move for a two-month work assignment.
Mrs. Gable did not respond to that email.
Marcus found a temporary subletter and collected $1,200 for July.
The subletter moved in on July 1st without a signed agreement from Mrs. Gable.
Mrs. Gable sent a formal notice on July 5th demanding the subletter vacate immediately.
Marcus failed to pay the August rent on time, citing a delay in his work stipend.
Mrs. Gable sent a text message on August 3rd calling Marcus 'unreliable and irresponsible'.
dispute: Marcus wants Mrs. Gable to waive the late fee for August and acknowledge the sublet as a valid solution; Mrs. Gable wants Marcus to pay the late fee and sign a document admitting to a lease violation.
fault_rationale: Marcus unilaterally sublet without permission and missed a payment deadline; Mrs. Gable ignored a formal request for communication and used derogatory language in a text.

title: The Late Rent Increase Notice
background: Marcus has lived in Elena's condo for two years under a month-to-month agreement.
facts: 1. The lease requires 30 days' notice for any rent changes.
2. Elena sent a notice to increase rent by $100 starting June 1st.
3. The notice was delivered on May 10th.
4. Marcus replied on May 12th asking for a compromise.
5. Elena told Marcus via text she would consider his request by May 15th.
6. Elena did not contact Marcus again until June 1st.
7. Marcus paid the old rent amount on June 1st.
8. Elena sent a formal demand for the $100 difference on June 2nd.
9. Marcus sent a response calling Elena's communication 'unprofessional and deceptive'.
dispute: Marcus wants to pay the old rate for June due to the lack of response; Elena wants the $100 increase paid immediately.
fault_rationale: Elena missed her promised follow-up deadline (Fact 5/6), while Marcus unilaterally decided to ignore the legal notice and used hostile language (Fact 7/9).

title: The Unreturned Apartment Key
background: Marcus moved out of Mrs. Gable's rental unit on October 31st.
facts: 1. The lease required keys to be returned by October 31st.
2. Marcus left the unit on October 31st without returning the key.
3. Marcus texted Mrs. Gable on November 1st stating he would mail the key by November 3rd.
4. Mrs. Gable replied on November 2nd that she would not accept mailed keys and demanded a hand-delivery.
5. Marcus did not respond to that text for four days.
6. Mrs. Gable changed the locks on November 6th.
7. Marcus mailed the key via certified mail on November 7th.
8. Mrs. Gable received the key on November 9th.
9. The cost of the lock change was $120.
10. Mrs. Gable deducted $120 from Marcus's security deposit.
dispute: Marcus wants the $120 deduction refunded; Mrs. Gable wants to keep the funds to cover the lock change.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the return deadline and ignored a text; Mrs. Gable unilaterally changed the locks before the mailed key could arrive.

title: The Bathroom Leak Dispute
background: A leak in the upstairs bathroom has caused water damage to the ceiling below.
facts: On October 1, Marcus notified Elena via text that the bathroom faucet was dripping.
Elena replied that she would send a plumber by October 5.
No plumber arrived by October 5.
On October 10, Marcus noticed water pooling on the floor and stopped using the faucet.
On October 12, Marcus hired a local handyman for $150 to patch the leak without notifying Elena.
The patch failed on October 15, resulting in a flood that damaged the downstairs ceiling.
Elena discovered the flood on October 16 during a scheduled inspection.
Marcus sent a message to Elena on October 17 calling her 'negligent' and 'unprofessional'.
Elena refused to reimburse Marcus for the $150 handyman fee.
dispute: Marcus wants reimbursement for the handyman and a rent reduction for the month; Elena wants Marcus to pay for the downstairs ceiling repairs.
fault_rationale: Elena missed her deadline to fix the initial leak, while Marcus made a unilateral repair and used hostile language.

title: The Shared Driveway Dispute
background: Marcus rents a unit from Elena; the lease includes one shared driveway spot that they agreed to alternate weekly.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed in writing to switch the parking spot every Sunday evening.
2. On September 1st, Marcus failed to move his car on Sunday evening.
3. Elena sent a text on September 2nd stating Marcus was 'stealing' her space.
4. Elena moved Marcus's car to the street using a tow service on September 3rd.
5. The lease states that towing is only permitted for unauthorized vehicles or emergencies.
6. Marcus did not pay the towing fee of $75.
7. Elena promised in a July email to waive the parking fee if Marcus helped with landscaping.
8. Marcus did not complete the agreed-upon landscaping work in August.
dispute: Marcus wants reimbursement for the towing fee; Elena wants the unpaid parking fee and the landscaping completed.
fault_rationale: Marcus broke the parking rotation and the landscaping agreement; Elena used a rude tone and towed a tenant's car in violation of the lease.

title: Living Room Painting Dispute
background: Marcus requested to paint the beige living room walls a neutral light grey.
facts: Sarah gave written permission for the color change on May 1st.
Sarah requested that Marcus provide the specific paint brand and code before starting.
Marcus painted the room light grey on May 10th without sending the paint code.
Marcus told Sarah via text on May 11th that he used a professional-grade matte finish.
Sarah visited the property on May 15th and stated the grey color was too dark.
Marcus agreed in a text on May 16th to repaint the walls beige before his lease ended.
Marcus moved out on July 31st without repainting the walls.
Sarah deducted $400 from the security deposit for professional repainting.
dispute: Marcus wants the $400 deduction refunded; Sarah wants to keep the money to cover the cost of restoring the original wall color.
fault_rationale: Marcus unilaterally ignored the paint code request and broke his promise to repaint; Sarah approved the change in principle but then subjectively rejected the color after the work was done.

title: Unannounced Landlord Entry
background: Marcus rents an apartment from Sarah under a written lease agreement.
facts: The lease states the landlord must provide 24 hours' notice before entering the unit.
Sarah entered the apartment on Tuesday at 2:00 PM without notifying Marcus.
Marcus arrived home at 2:15 PM and found Sarah inside the unit.
Sarah stated she wanted to check the water heater for a potential leak.
Marcus told Sarah he was upset that she entered without notice.
Sarah stated she forgot to send the text message due to a busy workday.
Marcus requested a written apology and a commitment to follow the lease.
Sarah stated that the entry was necessary for maintenance and no apology is needed.
dispute: Marcus wants a written apology and confirmation of future lease compliance; Sarah wants Marcus to accept the entry as a reasonable maintenance check.
fault_rationale: Sarah breached the explicit 24-hour notice agreement in the lease, while Marcus's only lapse is expressing annoyance.

title: Late Apartment Availability
background: Sarah signed a lease to move into Marcus's apartment on September 1st.
facts: The lease agreement specifies a move-in date of September 1st.
Sarah paid the first month's rent and security deposit on August 15th.
Marcus texted Sarah on August 30th stating the previous tenant had not yet vacated.
Sarah asked Marcus for an updated move-in timeline on August 31st.
Marcus did not respond to Sarah's message until September 3rd.
Marcus provided Sarah with the keys on September 5th.
Sarah stayed in a hotel from September 1st to September 5th.
Marcus stated he forgot to check the previous tenant's move-out status.
dispute: Marcus wants Sarah to pay the full rent for September; Sarah wants a pro-rated refund for the five days she could not access the unit.
fault_rationale: Marcus breached the explicit lease date and failed to communicate, while Sarah followed all contractual obligations.

title: Roommate Lease Addition Dispute
background: Marcus needs a roommate to cover rent; Sarah has agreed to move in and be added to the official lease.
facts: 1. Marcus and Sarah agreed on October 1st that Sarah would move in on November 1st.
2. Marcus told Sarah he would submit the lease addition paperwork to the landlord by October 15th.
3. Marcus did not submit the paperwork by October 15th.
4. Sarah sent Marcus a security deposit check on October 10th.
5. Marcus informed Sarah on October 20th that the landlord required an updated credit check from her.
6. Sarah did not send the credit check documents until November 2nd.
7. Sarah moved her furniture into the apartment on November 1st without a signed lease.
8. Marcus sent a text on November 3rd stating Sarah cannot stay until the landlord approves the application.
9. The landlord has not yet reviewed the application.
dispute: Marcus wants Sarah to move her belongings out until the lease is signed; Sarah wants to remain in the apartment since she already paid the deposit.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the paperwork deadline; Sarah missed the credit check deadline and moved in unilaterally.

title: The Cancelled August Trip
background: Marcus requested a week off in August for a family trip, which Sarah approved via email in May.
facts: 1. Sarah emailed approval for Marcus's August 12-19 vacation on May 15.
2. Marcus paid a non-refundable $1,200 deposit for flights on May 20.
3. Marcus missed the June 1 deadline to submit the project handover documentation.
4. Sarah did not follow up on the missing documentation until August 1.
5. A primary client moved a critical project deadline to August 15.
6. Sarah told Marcus on August 3 that he must cancel his vacation to lead the project.
7. Marcus replied to Sarah's request via text using all caps and calling the decision 'insane'.
8. Sarah offered to pay for the flight refund if Marcus worked the week.
dispute: Marcus wants the original vacation time and the company to pay for his lost deposit; Sarah wants Marcus to work the project deadline.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed a concrete deadline and sent a rude message; Sarah made a unilateral decision to cancel an approved leave with short notice.

title: Credit for the Quarterly Logistics Report
background: Sarah was tasked with creating a logistics efficiency report for Marcus to present to the board.
facts: 1. Marcus told Sarah on March 1st that she would be listed as the primary author of the report.
2. Sarah missed the internal draft deadline on March 15th.
3. Marcus completed the final data analysis and executive summary himself on March 20th.
4. Sarah sent an email on March 21st requesting a two-day extension for her final review.
5. Marcus submitted the report to the board on March 22nd without Sarah's name on the cover page.
6. Marcus attributed the work to 'Management' in the presentation slides.
7. Sarah sent a message to Marcus on March 23rd calling his actions 'unprofessional and deceptive'.
8. Sarah provided 80% of the raw research and formatting for the document.
dispute: Sarah wants her name added to the archived report as primary author; Marcus wants Sarah to apologize for her tone and accept the current attribution.
fault_rationale: Sarah missed a deadline and used rude language; Marcus broke a promise regarding authorship and made a unilateral decision to omit her name.

title: The Friday Shift Conflict
background: Marcus works a part-time retail position with a schedule usually set two weeks in advance.
facts: On October 1st, Sarah and Marcus agreed Marcus would be off every Friday in November.
On October 15th, Sarah emailed Marcus stating she needed him to work the following Friday, November 1st.
Marcus did not respond to the October 15th email.
On October 25th, Sarah updated the digital master schedule to show Marcus working every Friday in November.
Marcus noticed the schedule change on October 28th.
Marcus sent a text to Sarah on October 28th stating, 'I can't work Fridays, you already promised.'
Sarah replied on October 29th that the store is understaffed and the shift is mandatory.
Marcus did not show up for his shift on November 1st.
dispute: Marcus wants his original Friday-off agreement honored; Sarah wants Marcus to work the shifts and accept a formal warning for the no-show.
fault_rationale: Marcus ignored a direct email and skipped a scheduled shift; Sarah unilaterally changed a prior agreement and failed to confirm Marcus's availability.

title: Probationary Period Performance Review
background: Mark is completing a three-month probation period for a remote data analyst role.
facts: 1. Sarah and Mark signed an employment contract stating a core working hour requirement of 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM EST.
2. The contract specifies that all employees must be available on the company Slack channel during these hours.
3. On October 12, Sarah sent Mark five messages between 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM.
4. Mark did not respond to these messages until 7:00 PM that evening.
5. Sarah sent a written warning to Mark on October 13 regarding his availability.
6. On October 15, Mark was absent from Slack from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM without prior notice.
7. Mark stated he was taking a nap due to insomnia from the previous night.
8. Sarah scheduled a probation review meeting for October 20.
9. Sarah informed Mark during the meeting that his probation would not be confirmed due to reliability issues.
dispute: Sarah wants to terminate Mark's employment for breach of contract; Mark wants to be confirmed in his role with a warning.
fault_rationale: Mark violated the explicit core hours agreement twice (Facts 3, 6); Sarah followed the contract and provided a written warning (Fact 5).

title: Disputed Client Dinner Reimbursement
background: Marcus hosted a dinner for a prospective client to secure a new contract.
facts: The company policy requires pre-approval for any single meal over $150.
Marcus spent $280 on the dinner on October 12.
Marcus did not request pre-approval for the expense.
Sarah told Marcus on October 14 that she would review the receipt by Friday.
Friday passed without a response or payment from Sarah.
Marcus sent a follow-up email on Monday morning.
Sarah replied to the email by stating the reimbursement was denied due to the lack of pre-approval.
Marcus replied to Sarah's denial using all capital letters and calling her 'incompetent'.
The prospective client signed a $5,000 contract with the company on October 20.
dispute: Marcus wants full reimbursement of the $280; Sarah wants the claim denied due to policy violations and conduct.
fault_rationale: Marcus bypassed the approval policy and sent a rude message; Sarah missed her promised deadline for review.

title: The Non-Compete Reminder
background: Marcus is a senior designer at Elena's boutique agency who is transitioning to a freelance role.
facts: Marcus signed a non-compete agreement limiting client poaching for twelve months after departure.
Elena promised Marcus in writing a flexible transition period to maintain a few small legacy clients.
Marcus missed the final project deadline for the agency's largest account by four days.
Elena failed to pay Marcus's final commission check on the agreed date of October 1st.
Marcus began promoting his new independent studio on LinkedIn while still on the agency payroll.
Elena sent a formal email reminding Marcus of his non-compete restrictions two weeks before his departure.
Marcus ignored three follow-up emails from Elena regarding the handover of client files.
Elena unilaterally reduced Marcus's access to the company server three days before his official end date.
dispute: Marcus wants his unpaid commission and a written waiver for his specific legacy clients; Elena wants a signed confirmation that Marcus will not contact any agency clients for one year.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed a major deadline and ignored handover emails; Elena withheld pay and cut server access prematurely.

title: Work Requests During Medical Leave
background: Elena is on a doctor-mandated two-week sick leave for recovery from a minor surgical procedure.
facts: Marcus and Elena agreed in writing on October 1st that Elena would be completely offline during her leave.
Elena began her medical leave on October 3rd.
Marcus sent Elena five emails and three urgent text messages between October 4th and October 6th requesting a client report.
Elena did not respond to the messages.
Marcus called Elena's personal phone on October 7th.
Elena answered the call and told Marcus she was unable to work per the agreement.
Marcus stated that the client had a deadline and the files were only on Elena's computer.
Marcus told Elena he would not approve her paid leave for that week if she did not send the files.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to provide the files immediately to satisfy the client; Elena wants Marcus to honor the original agreement and pay her leave.
fault_rationale: Marcus violated a written agreement and threatened legal pay; Elena committed no lapse by following the agreed-upon leave.

title: Internal Transfer Dispute
background: Marcus requested a transfer to the Product team to align with his career goals.
facts: 1. Marcus submitted a formal transfer request on September 1.
2. Sarah told Marcus via email on September 15 that she would approve the transfer once the current project ended on October 1.
3. Marcus missed two project deadlines in the final week of September.
4. On October 2, Sarah informed Marcus that the transfer was delayed until November 1.
5. Marcus sent a message to Sarah on October 3 stating she was 'obstructing his career'.
6. Sarah moved Marcus's current files to a shared folder without notifying him on October 4.
7. The Product team lead emailed Sarah on October 5 stating they had an immediate opening for Marcus.
8. Sarah did not respond to that email for four business days.
dispute: Marcus wants an immediate transfer to the Product team; Sarah wants Marcus to remain in his current role until November 1 to ensure a clean handover.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed deadlines and sent a rude message; Sarah broke her promise regarding the date and ignored a stakeholder email.

title: The Overdue Client Presentation
background: Marcus is a lead designer tasked with creating a pitch deck for a major client, supervised by Elena.
facts: 1. Elena told Marcus on Monday that the final deck was due Friday at 5:00 PM.
2. Marcus requested specific brand assets from Elena on Tuesday morning.
3. Elena did not send the assets until Thursday afternoon.
4. Marcus emailed Elena on Thursday at 6:00 PM stating he would need until Monday to finish properly.
5. Elena replied on Friday morning saying the deadline remained Friday at 5:00 PM.
6. Marcus submitted the deck on Friday at 5:00 PM with several missing slides.
7. The client emailed Elena on Friday evening complaining about the incomplete presentation.
8. Elena sent a formal reprimand to Marcus on Monday morning.
dispute: Marcus wants the reprimand removed from his file; Elena wants Marcus to take full accountability for the client's dissatisfaction.
fault_rationale: Elena failed to provide necessary assets promptly; Marcus submitted incomplete work despite knowing the deadline.

title: The Notice Period Conflict
background: Marcus is a project manager resigning from a small agency to join a competitor.
facts: The employment contract specifies a four-week notice period.
Marcus told Sarah verbally three months ago he would likely leave by year-end.
Sarah told Marcus in writing last month that she would waive the notice period if he found a new role.
Marcus submitted his formal resignation on November 1st with a final date of November 15th.
Sarah sent an email on November 2nd stating she now requires the full four weeks to hand over clients.
Marcus missed two client status meetings during his final two weeks.
Sarah withheld Marcus's final discretionary bonus in the last payroll cycle.
The company handbook states bonuses are subject to 'satisfactory completion of duties'.
dispute: Marcus wants his final bonus and to leave on November 15th; Sarah wants Marcus to work until November 29th to receive the bonus.
fault_rationale: Marcus failed to attend required meetings; Sarah reneged on her written promise to waive the notice period.

title: Shared Lease Termination Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena are ex-partners who signed a one-year lease together and are now separating.
facts: The lease expires in three months.
Marcus and Elena agreed in writing to find a replacement tenant to avoid a buyout fee.
Elena promised to list the apartment on three platforms by October 1st.
Elena did not post the listing until October 12th.
Marcus decided to paint the living room a dark grey on October 15th without consulting Elena.
The landlord requires all applicants to be screened by a specific agency.
Marcus referred a friend as a replacement tenant but did not tell the friend to use the required agency.
Elena sent a text message to the potential replacement tenant calling them 'unreliable' after a viewing.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to pay the full lease buyout fee because her listing delay lost them a prime window; Elena wants Marcus to pay the fee because his unilateral painting and poor referral process deterred quality tenants.
fault_rationale: Elena missed the agreed listing deadline and insulted a candidate; Marcus made a unilateral aesthetic change and ignored the landlord's screening process.

title: The Shared Album Dispute
background: Maya and Liam ended a three-year relationship four months ago and shared a joint cloud photo album.
facts: 1. Maya and Liam agreed during the breakup to delete all photos of each other from social media by September 1st.
2. On August 15th, Liam deleted his public Instagram posts featuring Maya.
3. On August 20th, Maya posted a new photo of herself and her dog, tagging the location as their former shared apartment.
4. On September 2nd, Maya requested that Liam remove three specific group photos from the shared cloud album that he still manages.
5. Liam did not respond to the request for ten days.
6. On September 12th, Liam archived the entire shared cloud album, making it inaccessible to Maya.
7. Maya sent Liam a text message on September 13th calling him 'pathetic' for hiding the photos.
8. Liam stated he archived the album because Maya had not yet deleted the old profile picture of them together on her Facebook page.
dispute: Maya wants the cloud album restored so she can download her personal photos; Liam wants Maya to delete the final couple's photo on Facebook before he restores access.
fault_rationale: Maya missed the deletion deadline and sent a rude message; Liam missed the request deadline and unilaterally revoked access to shared data.

title: The Returned Anniversary Tablet
background: Maya and Liam broke up two months ago after a three-year relationship.
facts: Liam bought Maya a $500 tablet for their anniversary last year.
Liam paid for the tablet using a joint credit account they shared.
Maya promised Liam she would pay half of the cost back within one month.
Maya did not pay the $250 back to the joint account.
Liam sent Maya three texts asking for the money in November.
Maya ignored those texts for three weeks.
Liam contacted the retailer and initiated a return for the tablet using the original purchase credentials.
The retailer shipped the tablet back to Liam's address.
dispute: Maya wants the tablet returned to her because it was a gift; Liam wants to keep the tablet and return the funds to the joint account.
fault_rationale: Maya broke a financial promise and ignored communication; Liam made a unilateral decision to revoke a gift through a third party.

title: The Shared Car Loan Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena ended their relationship six months ago but remained jointly responsible for a car loan.
facts: Marcus and Elena signed a joint loan for a 2021 sedan.
The couple agreed in writing that Elena would keep the car and make the monthly payments.
Elena missed two consecutive payments in October and November.
Marcus paid those two missed installments to prevent a credit hit.
Elena sent a text message in December calling Marcus 'controlling' regarding the car.
Marcus removed the spare key and the emergency roadside kit from the vehicle without notifying Elena.
Elena has not reimbursed Marcus for the October and November payments.
Marcus requested that Elena refinance the loan into her name alone by January 1st.
Elena did not complete the refinancing application by the January deadline.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to pay him back immediately and refinance the loan by the end of the week; Elena wants Marcus to return the car accessories before she agrees to a new refinancing timeline.
fault_rationale: Elena missed payments and deadlines; Marcus unilaterally removed property and sent a demanding ultimatum.

title: The Shared Friend's Birthday Party
background: Leo and Maya broke up four months ago but share a close friend group.
facts: 1. Their mutual friend, Sarah, invited both Leo and Maya to her birthday party on Saturday.
2. Leo and Maya agreed via text to coordinate their arrival times to avoid an awkward encounter.
3. Leo told Maya he would arrive at 8:00 PM if she arrived at 9:00 PM.
4. Maya sent a text to Leo on Friday stating she had changed her mind and would arrive at 8:00 PM instead.
5. Leo did not respond to Maya's Friday text.
6. Leo arrived at the party at 8:00 PM.
7. Maya arrived at the party at 8:00 PM.
8. Maya told Sarah in front of other guests that Leo had ignored her coordination text.
9. Leo told the group that Maya had unilaterally changed the plan at the last minute.
dispute: Leo wants Maya to apologize for embarrassing him in front of their friends; Maya wants Leo to admit he ignored her message and apologize for the clash.
fault_rationale: Leo lapsed by ignoring the Friday text; Maya lapsed by unilaterally changing the agreed time and publicly criticizing Leo.

title: Shared Care for Buster the Dog
background: Marcus and Elena broke up six months ago but share joint ownership of their dog, Buster.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed to split all vet bills 50/50.
2. Elena took Buster to the vet for a skin condition on October 12th.
3. The total bill was $450.
4. Elena sent Marcus a request for $225 on October 13th.
5. Marcus did not pay the request or respond to the message for three weeks.
6. On November 3rd, Elena scheduled a follow-up appointment without notifying Marcus.
7. Marcus sent Elena a text on November 4th calling her 'controlling' and 'manipulative'.
8. Marcus paid the original $225 on November 5th.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to consult him before all future appointments; Elena wants Marcus to pay for the follow-up visit immediately.
fault_rationale: Marcus failed to pay a bill for three weeks and used insulting language; Elena made a medical decision unilaterally without notifying the co-owner.

title: Storage Unit Access Dispute
background: Maya and Liam broke up six months ago and share a storage unit containing both of their belongings.
facts: 1. Maya and Liam signed a written agreement on July 1st to share the monthly cost of the unit.
2. The agreement stated Liam would not remove Maya's items without her written consent.
3. Maya paid her portion of the rent for July, August, and September.
4. Liam stopped paying his portion of the rent in August.
5. On October 10th, Liam entered the unit and removed Maya's furniture and boxes.
6. Liam did not notify Maya before removing the items.
7. Liam told Maya he moved her things to a basement because he could no longer afford the unit.
8. Maya requested the return of her items on October 12th.
9. Liam stated he cannot move the items back until next month due to his current lack of transportation.
dispute: Maya wants Liam to return her belongings immediately; Liam wants Maya to wait until he has a vehicle.
fault_rationale: Liam breached the written agreement and removed items without consent, whereas Maya adhered to all payment and communication terms.

title: The Apartment Exit Date
background: Marcus and Elena are ex-partners who shared a leased apartment and are now coordinating their final move-out dates.
facts: 1. The lease expires on September 30.
2. Marcus and Elena agreed on August 1 to finalize a moving schedule by August 15.
3. Marcus did not send a proposed schedule by August 15.
4. Elena informed Marcus on August 20 that she would be moving out on September 15.
5. Elena decided the September 15 date without consulting Marcus.
6. Marcus requested to stay until September 30 to save on double-rent costs.
7. Elena sent a text to Marcus on August 22 calling his request 'selfish'.
8. Marcus promised to pay for the professional cleaning service if Elena left by the 15th.
9. Marcus has not yet paid the cleaning deposit required to book the service.
dispute: Marcus wants to stay until September 30; Elena wants him to vacate by September 15.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the planning deadline and the cleaning payment; Elena made a unilateral move-out decision and used derogatory language.

title: Joint Savings Division
background: Marcus and Elena shared a joint savings account for three years to save for a home before breaking up four months ago.
facts: 1. The account currently holds $12,000.
2. Marcus contributed $7,000 and Elena contributed $5,000.
3. Three months ago, Marcus and Elena agreed in writing to split the funds proportionally.
4. Marcus promised to initiate the transfer by the 1st of last month.
5. Marcus did not initiate the transfer by the 1st of last month.
6. Two weeks ago, Elena withdrew $1,000 from the account without notifying Marcus.
7. Elena stated the withdrawal was for an urgent car repair.
8. Marcus sent a text message to Elena yesterday calling her 'untrustworthy' and 'a thief'.
9. Elena has not responded to Marcus's last three emails regarding the final split.
dispute: Marcus wants a proportional split based on the original $12,000 balance; Elena wants a 50/50 split of the remaining $11,000 to compensate for Marcus's delay.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the agreed deadline and sent a rude message; Elena made a unilateral withdrawal and is now ignoring communication.

title: The Borrowed Laptop Dispute
background: Marcus borrowed Elena's laptop for a freelance project after they broke up.
facts: 1. Elena lent Marcus her laptop on June 1st.
2. Marcus agreed in writing to return the laptop by June 15th.
3. Marcus did not return the laptop on June 15th.
4. Elena sent a text reminder on June 16th.
5. Marcus responded on June 17th that he needed three more days.
6. Marcus did not return the laptop by June 20th.
7. Marcus stated he forgot to bring it to the meeting on June 21st.
8. Elena requested the laptop again on June 22nd.
9. Marcus currently possesses the laptop.
dispute: Marcus wants to keep the laptop for one more week to finish his project; Elena wants the laptop returned immediately.
fault_rationale: Marcus breached the explicit return date and subsequent extension; Elena has only requested her property back.

title: The Shared Driveway Maintenance Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena share a private driveway that requires periodic gravel replenishment and grading to remain usable.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed in writing to split the cost of driveway maintenance 50/50.
2. In March, Marcus hired a contractor to grade the driveway without notifying Elena.
3. Marcus sent Elena a bill for $400 for the March work.
4. Elena paid $200 to Marcus two weeks after the deadline specified in the bill.
5. In June, Elena noticed a large pothole forming in the shared section.
6. Elena messaged Marcus on July 1st requesting he coordinate a repair.
7. Marcus did not respond to the July 1st message.
8. On July 15th, Elena paid a contractor $300 to fill the pothole.
9. Elena sent Marcus a request for $150 to cover his share of the July repair.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to pay the remaining $200 from the March work before he pays for July; Elena wants Marcus to pay the $150 for the July repair immediately.
fault_rationale: Marcus made a unilateral decision and ignored a communication; Elena missed a payment deadline and performed a repair without prior coordination.

title: The Shared Driveway Remodel
background: Marcus is replacing his driveway, which requires heavy machinery and noise adjacent to Elena's home office.
facts: 1. Marcus agreed to limit heavy machinery use to between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM.
2. On Tuesday, Marcus's contractors operated a jackhammer until 7:30 PM.
3. Elena requested that Marcus provide 48 hours' notice before any high-noise phases.
4. Marcus sent a text notification for the final grading phase two hours before it began.
5. Elena blocked the shared access path with her vehicle for four hours during a scheduled pour day.
6. The construction project has extended two weeks past the original estimated completion date.
7. Elena sent a group email to the neighborhood association complaining about the noise before speaking to Marcus.
8. Marcus stopped responding to Elena's text messages for three days following the email.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to keep the shared path clear regardless of notice; Elena wants a formal written schedule and a financial credit for the noise disturbance.
fault_rationale: Marcus broke the time agreement and failed the notice period; Elena obstructed the work site and escalated the conflict via the HOA prematurely.

title: The Weekend Leaf Blower Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena live in adjacent houses with a shared property line and a common agreement to keep the shared alleyway clear of debris.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed last month to split the cost of a professional leaf removal service.
2. Elena decided to buy her own high-powered leaf blower instead of hiring the service.
3. Elena used the blower for three hours starting at 7:00 AM on Sunday.
4. Marcus sent Elena a text message at 7:15 AM calling her 'inconsiderate' and 'obnoxious'.
5. Elena blew a large pile of leaves from her yard onto Marcus's lawn.
6. Marcus promised to trim the overhanging hedge that blocks Elena's access to the alley by October 1st.
7. It is currently October 15th and the hedge remains untrimmed.
8. Marcus told Elena he would no longer speak to her until she apologized for the noise.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to commit to specific 'quiet hours' and stop blowing leaves onto his property; Elena wants Marcus to trim the hedge as promised before she considers any one-sided noise restrictions.
fault_rationale: Elena made a unilateral decision on the service and disturbed the peace/encroached on property; Marcus failed to meet a deadline for the hedge and used hostile language.

title: The Overgrown Boundary Hedge
background: Marcus and Elena share a property line marked by a tall privet hedge that requires annual pruning to prevent it from blocking light and encroaching on walkways.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed in March to split the $200 cost of a professional trimmer.
2. Elena hired the trimmer in April and paid the full $200 upfront.
3. Marcus did not reimburse Elena for his share of the cost by the agreed May 1st deadline.
4. In June, Marcus pruned the hedge on his side of the line without notifying Elena.
5. Marcus cut the hedge back further than the property line, removing branches on Elena's side.
6. Elena sent a text message to Marcus calling his actions 'reckless and amateur'.
7. Elena pruned her side of the hedge in August, leaving the branches uneven with Marcus's side.
8. Marcus told Elena he would not pay the original $200 because she 'ruined' the hedge's shape.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to professionally level the hedge at her own expense; Elena wants Marcus to pay the $100 debt from April.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed a payment deadline and unilaterally pruned Elena's property; Elena used hostile language and performed an asymmetrical pruning.

title: The Shared Driveway Bin Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena share a narrow driveway and a designated waste collection area at the curb.
facts: Marcus and Elena agreed in June to split the curb space equally for their bins.
Elena's bin is three feet wider than the agreed-upon boundary.
Marcus sent a text on July 1st asking Elena to move her bin.
Elena replied she would move it by Sunday, but the bin remained in place.
On July 10th, Marcus moved Elena's bin to the opposite side of the driveway without notifying her.
The new placement blocked the path for Elena's recycling pickup.
Elena sent a message calling Marcus 'unreasonable' and 'petty'.
Marcus ceased responding to all messages from Elena for two weeks.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to strictly adhere to the original boundary line; Elena wants Marcus to stop moving her property and apologize for the tone of the conflict.
fault_rationale: Elena broke the boundary agreement and a promised deadline; Marcus made a unilateral decision to move property and then ghosted the neighbor.

title: The Shared Property Line Drone Incident
background: Marcus and Sarah share a narrow alleyway between their houses and have a casual agreement to coordinate property maintenance.
facts: Marcus purchased a high-resolution photography drone.
Marcus and Sarah agreed on June 1st that Marcus would only fly the drone on weekends.
On Tuesday, June 12th, Marcus flew the drone over Sarah's backyard for thirty minutes.
Sarah requested Marcus stop flying the drone on June 13th.
Marcus promised Sarah he would install a physical privacy screen on the shared fence by June 30th.
June 30th passed without Marcus installing the screen.
On July 5th, Sarah moved a heavy shared storage bin into the alleyway, blocking Marcus's designated drone launch area.
Sarah sent a text message to Marcus on July 6th calling him 'unreliable and inconsiderate'.
Marcus requested Sarah move the bin by July 7th.
dispute: Marcus wants the storage bin moved immediately; Sarah wants a written guarantee that the drone will not fly on weekdays and the screen will be installed.
fault_rationale: Marcus violated the weekday flight agreement and missed the screen deadline; Sarah unilaterally blocked the launch area and used insulting language.

title: The Shared Boundary Sprinkler
background: Marcus and Elena share a property line containing a common garden strip.
facts: 1. Marcus and Elena agreed in May to split the cost of a new automatic sprinkler system.
2. Elena paid the full $300 installation fee upfront.
3. Marcus promised to reimburse Elena $150 by June 1st.
4. Marcus did not send the payment by June 1st.
5. Marcus sent a text on June 15th stating he would pay next week.
6. Elena changed the sprinkler timer to run at 5:00 AM without notifying Marcus.
7. The 5:00 AM setting wakes Marcus up every morning.
8. Marcus moved the sprinkler head to focus exclusively on his side of the garden.
9. Marcus has not yet paid the $150.
dispute: Marcus wants the timer moved back to 8:00 AM; Elena wants the $150 reimbursement and the sprinkler head returned to the center.
fault_rationale: Marcus failed to meet the payment deadline and unilaterally moved the hardware; Elena changed the schedule without consultation.

title: Shared Driveway Light Installation
background: Marcus and Sarah share a private driveway that splits between their two properties.
facts: 1. Marcus and Sarah agreed on November 1st that no decorations would block the shared driveway.
2. Sarah installed a small wreath on her porch on November 5th.
3. Marcus installed a large light display across the driveway entrance on December 1st.
4. The display requires cars to drive over a thick power cable to enter the driveway.
5. Sarah asked Marcus to move the cable on December 2nd.
6. Marcus stated he could not move it because the extension cord was too short.
7. The cable has been run over by Sarah's car ten times.
8. Sarah requested Marcus remove the lights by December 5th.
9. Marcus refused to remove the lights until after December 25th.
dispute: Marcus wants to keep the lights up until Christmas; Sarah wants the lights removed immediately.
fault_rationale: Marcus broke the explicit agreement and created a hazard; Sarah only made reasonable requests for removal.

title: The Unleashed Dog Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena share a boundary fence with a small gap at the bottom.
facts: 1. Marcus agreed to keep his dog on a leash in the shared alleyway.
2. Elena asked Marcus to fix the gap in the fence by October 1st.
3. Marcus did not fix the fence by October 1st.
4. On October 5th, Marcus's dog entered Elena's yard through the gap without a leash.
5. Elena caught the dog and held it for two hours before calling Marcus.
6. Marcus sent a text message calling Elena 'unreasonable' for not calling him immediately.
7. Elena told Marcus she would no longer notify him if the dog entered her yard.
8. Marcus asked Elena to stop trapping his dog.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to return the dog immediately upon entry and stop 'trapping' him; Elena wants Marcus to fix the fence and ensure the dog is always leashed.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the fence repair deadline and sent a rude message; Elena broke the implied agreement to notify him immediately and made a unilateral decision to stop communicating.

title: Security Deposit Dispute
background: Liam and Maya moved out of a shared apartment and received a $1,200 refund from the landlord, minus $300 for a hole in the bedroom wall.
facts: 1. Liam and Maya each paid $600 for the initial security deposit.
2. Liam agreed to patch the bedroom wall before the final inspection.
3. Liam did not patch the wall before moving out.
4. Maya agreed to handle the final utility bill payment.
5. Maya missed the utility deadline, resulting in a $50 late fee.
6. The landlord deducted $300 from the deposit for the wall damage.
7. Maya received the $900 refund check in her bank account.
8. Maya sent Liam $400 via Venmo two days after the refund arrived.
9. Liam sent Maya a text stating the $400 payment was insufficient.
dispute: Liam wants $450 more to split the remaining refund equally; Maya wants Liam to absorb the full $300 wall deduction since he failed to fix it.
fault_rationale: Liam failed to perform the agreed repair; Maya missed a financial deadline and unilaterally decided the deposit split.

title: The Weekend Guest Dispute
background: Marcus and Chloe share a two-bedroom apartment and agreed to a 'no guests for more than two nights' rule without prior notice.
facts: 1. Marcus and Chloe signed a roommate agreement stating guests are limited to two nights.
2. On Friday, Marcus texted Chloe that his partner was staying over for the weekend.
3. Chloe replied to that text with 'K' and did not explicitly object.
4. Marcus's partner remained in the apartment from Friday through Tuesday morning.
5. Chloe asked Marcus on Sunday to tell his partner to leave by Monday morning.
6. Marcus told Chloe he would handle it on Sunday night.
7. Marcus's partner stayed Monday night.
8. On Tuesday, Chloe sent a group text to Marcus and his partner calling Marcus 'selfish' and 'disrespectful'.
9. Chloe had a friend stay over for four consecutive nights three weeks ago.
dispute: Marcus wants Chloe to apologize for the rude group text; Chloe wants Marcus to agree to a stricter, written guest penalty system.
fault_rationale: Marcus broke the agreement and a specific promise to remove the guest; Chloe violated the same agreement previously and used a rude communication method.

title: Kitchen Cleaning Dispute
background: Maya and Liam share a two-bedroom apartment and agreed to a rotating weekly cleaning schedule for the common areas.
facts: Maya and Liam signed a written agreement to alternate deep-cleaning the kitchen every Sunday.
On October 1st, it was Liam's turn to clean the kitchen.
Liam did not clean the kitchen on October 1st.
Liam sent a text to Maya on October 2nd stating he forgot due to work stress.
On October 8th, it was Maya's turn to clean the kitchen.
Maya cleaned the counters but did not mop the floors or clean the microwave.
On October 15th, Liam cleaned the kitchen.
Maya sent a group chat message on October 16th calling Liam 'lazy and unreliable' regarding the October 1st lapse.
Liam decided on October 17th to stop using the shared cleaning supplies and bought his own set.
dispute: Maya wants Liam to apologize for the initial missed week and commit to a stricter schedule; Liam wants Maya to apologize for the insult and contribute money toward new shared supplies.
fault_rationale: Liam missed a scheduled cleaning and unilaterally stopped sharing supplies; Maya performed an incomplete cleaning and used insulting language.

title: The Lost Apartment Key
background: Marcus and Leo share a rental apartment and a single spare set of keys for the front door.
facts: Marcus and Leo agreed that the spare key would always remain on the kitchen counter.
Leo took the spare key to go for a walk on Tuesday.
Leo lost the spare key during his walk.
The landlord charges a $150 fee for lock replacement and a new key.
Marcus requested that Leo pay the full $150 fee.
Leo stated he was distracted by a phone call when the key fell out of his pocket.
Leo offered to pay $40 toward the fee.
Marcus has not paid the landlord yet.
dispute: Marcus wants Leo to pay the full $150 replacement fee; Leo wants to split the cost with Marcus.
fault_rationale: Leo violated the explicit agreement regarding the key's location and lost the item, while Marcus has made no lapse in behavior.

title: The Shared Pantry Conflict
background: Marcus and Chloe share a communal grocery fund for staples (milk, oil, eggs) and use a shared digital list for requests.
facts: 1. Marcus and Chloe agreed to split the cost of shared staples equally each month.
2. Chloe manages the grocery shopping and the shared fund.
3. On October 1st, Chloe bought $60 of shared staples.
4. Marcus did not pay his $30 share of the October 1st shop by the agreed October 5th deadline.
5. On October 12th, Marcus used the last of the shared milk without adding it to the digital list.
6. On October 14th, Chloe bought premium organic eggs for the household without consulting Marcus.
7. The organic eggs cost $12, which is triple the price of the usual brand.
8. Marcus sent a text message on October 15th calling Chloe's spending 'absurd and controlling'.
9. Marcus paid his $30 share for the October 1st shop on October 16th.
dispute: Marcus wants a $6 credit toward his next share due to the expensive eggs; Chloe wants Marcus to apologize for the text and commit to a stricter payment schedule.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed a payment deadline and used the last of a product without listing it; Chloe made a unilateral decision to buy expensive luxury items with shared funds.

title: The Cello Practice Dispute
background: Marcus and Elena share a two-bedroom apartment with a thin shared wall between the living room and Elena's bedroom.
facts: Elena plays the cello for a university ensemble.
Marcus and Elena agreed that Elena would practice only between 4:00 PM and 7:00 PM.
On Tuesday, Elena practiced from 8:00 PM to 10:00 PM.
Marcus works from home on a flexible schedule.
On Wednesday, Marcus told Elena she was 'being selfish' via a text message.
Elena promised to buy sound-dampening pads for her endpin by Friday.
Friday passed and Elena did not purchase the pads.
Marcus decided to move the shared living room coffee table into Elena's room without asking her on Saturday.
dispute: Marcus wants a written contract banning all instrument play after 7:00 PM; Elena wants Marcus to move the furniture back and apologize for the text.
fault_rationale: Elena broke the time agreement and the promise to buy pads; Marcus sent a rude message and made a unilateral decision regarding furniture.

title: The Lease Renewal Conflict
background: Maya and Liam have shared a two-bedroom apartment for one year; the lease expires in 30 days.
facts: The lease requires a renewal notice to the landlord by the first of the month.
Maya and Liam agreed on April 15th to discuss the renewal together on April 20th.
Liam did not attend the meeting on April 20th.
Maya sent a text to Liam on April 21st stating she would handle the renewal alone if he didn't respond.
Liam did not reply to that text for three days.
Maya signed the renewal lease for another year on April 24th without Liam's signature.
The new lease includes a $100 monthly rent increase per person.
Liam informed Maya on April 27th that he intended to move out at the end of the current lease.
Maya told Liam on April 28th that he is legally bound to the new lease.
dispute: Maya wants Liam to sign the new lease and pay his share of the rent; Liam wants to move out without being held to the new lease.
fault_rationale: Liam lapsed by missing the agreed meeting and failing to communicate; Maya lapsed by unilaterally signing a legal contract for another person.

title: The Inventory Expansion Conflict
background: Marcus manages the day-to-day operations of Elena's boutique home goods store.
facts: 1. Elena and Marcus agreed on June 1st that Marcus would handle the autumn inventory order.
2. Marcus missed the supplier deadline for the autumn collection on August 15th.
3. Elena discovered the missed deadline on August 20th.
4. Elena ordered $5,000 of replacement stock from a different vendor on August 21st without telling Marcus.
5. Marcus sent an email to Elena on August 22nd calling her management style 'suffocating'.
6. Elena told Marcus on August 23rd that he is no longer allowed to approve purchases over $200.
7. Marcus had promised to implement a new digital tracking system by July 1st.
8. The digital tracking system is not yet operational.
dispute: Marcus wants his purchasing autonomy restored; Elena wants Marcus to step down as manager.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed a supplier deadline and failed to implement the tracking system; Elena made a unilateral $5,000 purchase and stripped Marcus of his authority.

title: Coordination of Elder Care
background: Sarah and Mark are coordinating the weekly care and grocery needs for their father, who lives alone.
facts: Sarah and Mark agreed to split the weekly grocery shopping and delivery 50/50.
Sarah missed her scheduled delivery turn on October 12th.
Mark purchased a new automated medication dispenser for their father without consulting Sarah.
Sarah sent a text message to Mark on October 15th calling his decision 'controlling.'
Mark forgot to send Sarah the receipt for the medication dispenser as promised.
Sarah agreed to drive their father to a specialist appointment on October 20th.
Sarah cancelled the appointment 24 hours in advance due to a work conflict.
Mark spent three hours on Sunday cleaning their father's house.
dispute: Sarah wants Mark to stop making unilateral healthcare decisions; Mark wants Sarah to commit to the agreed-upon schedule without cancellations.
fault_rationale: Sarah missed a delivery and cancelled an appointment; Mark made a unilateral purchase and failed to provide a promised receipt.

title: The Post-Vacation Expense Split
background: Marcus and Elena took a joint trip to visit their parents in Florida and agreed to split shared costs equally.
facts: 1. Elena booked the shared Airbnb and paid the full $1,200 upfront.
2. Marcus agreed to pay Elena $600 for his half of the lodging by the trip's end.
3. Marcus paid for all group meals and gas during the week, totaling $850.
4. Elena used the group rental car to run personal errands for three hours on Tuesday.
5. Marcus did not reimburse Elena for the Airbnb by the agreed date.
6. Elena sent Marcus a text saying, 'You are irresponsible with money,' three days after the trip.
7. Marcus unilaterally decided to subtract $100 from his Airbnb payment to cover his share of the gas.
8. Elena refuses to acknowledge the meal expenses as part of the shared split.
dispute: Marcus wants Elena to deduct the meals/gas from the Airbnb cost; Elena wants the full $600 payment for the lodging.
fault_rationale: Marcus missed the payment deadline and made a unilateral financial decision; Elena used the shared car for personal use and sent a rude message.

title: The Sibling's Wedding Gift Fund
background: Sarah and Julian agreed to split a $600 luxury espresso machine for their brother's wedding.
facts: 1. Sarah and Julian agreed on June 1st to split the $600 cost equally.
2. Sarah agreed to purchase the item and be reimbursed by Julian.
3. The deadline for Julian to send his $300 share was July 1st.
4. Julian did not send the money by July 1st.
5. On July 5th, Sarah purchased the machine using her own credit card.
6. Sarah did not notify Julian that she had finalized the purchase.
7. Julian sent a text on July 10th stating he could only afford $150 currently.
8. Sarah replied to that text calling Julian 'irresponsible' and 'selfish'.
9. Julian has since paid Sarah $150.
dispute: Sarah wants the remaining $150 immediately; Julian wants Sarah to accept the $150 as his full contribution due to her rude communication and unilateral purchase.
fault_rationale: Julian missed the payment deadline and broke the cost agreement; Sarah purchased the item without confirmation and sent a derogatory message.

title: The Borrowed Heirloom Ring
background: Maya borrowed a gold family ring from Julian to wear to a formal gala.
facts: Julian lent Maya the ring on October 1st.
Julian requested the ring be returned by October 5th.
Maya sent a text on October 5th stating she would return it the following day.
Maya did not return the ring on October 6th.
Julian sent three follow-up messages between October 6th and October 10th.
Maya did not respond to those messages.
Maya returned the ring on October 12th.
The ring has a new scratch on the center stone.
Julian told Maya via text that he is blocking her number until she pays for a professional polishing.
dispute: Julian wants Maya to pay $100 for professional restoration; Maya wants Julian to apologize for blocking her and overreacting to a minor scratch.
fault_rationale: Maya broke the return deadline and ignored communications; Julian unilaterally cut off contact and demanded payment without an appraisal.

title: The House-Sitting Handover
background: Julian hired Maya to watch his home and water plants for three weeks while he traveled.
facts: 1. Julian and Maya agreed on a payment of $500 for the three-week period.
2. Julian told Maya via text to water the orchids every Monday.
3. Maya missed watering the orchids for two consecutive Mondays.
4. Julian returned home and found two orchids dead.
5. Maya sent a request for the $500 payment on the day she finished.
6. Julian did not respond to the payment request for ten days.
7. Maya sent a follow-up message calling Julian 'unprofessional' and 'cheap'.
8. Julian decided to deduct $100 from the payment to cover the cost of new plants.
dispute: Julian wants to pay Maya $400; Maya wants the full $500 payment immediately.
fault_rationale: Maya neglected the specific care instructions; Julian ignored the payment request and made a unilateral financial deduction.

title: The Down Payment Gift
background: Robert offered Elena $10,000 to help with a home down payment provided she shared the home's financial records.
facts: Robert told Elena in January he would gift her $10,000 for a house.
Robert requested a copy of the mortgage application and budget by March 1st.
Elena did not send the documents by March 1st.
Elena sent the documents on March 15th.
Robert transferred $5,000 to Elena on March 20th.
Robert told Elena via text on April 1st that he would not send the remaining $5,000.
Elena told Robert via text on April 2nd that he was being controlling.
Elena used the first $5,000 for a non-housing home improvement project.
dispute: Elena wants the remaining $5,000 gift; Robert wants Elena to repay the first $5,000.
fault_rationale: Elena missed the deadline and misused funds; Robert unilaterally revoked a promise based on a delay.

title: The Missed 30th Birthday Dinner
background: Sarah invited David to a celebratory dinner for her 30th birthday.
facts: Sarah told David the dinner was on Saturday at 7:00 PM.
David agreed to attend and said he would drive Sarah's brother.
Sarah sent a calendar invite to David two weeks prior.
David did not accept the calendar invite.
David arrived at the restaurant at 8:15 PM.
Sarah sent David a text at 7:15 PM asking where he was.
David replied to the text with a one-word answer: 'Traffic'.
Sarah left the restaurant before David arrived.
dispute: Sarah wants a sincere apology and acknowledgment of her feelings; David wants Sarah to acknowledge his effort to attend despite the delay.
fault_rationale: David broke his promise to arrive on time and sent a curt message; Sarah made a unilateral decision to leave before he arrived.
